item.text:
**7B.10 Research Note: Shehbaz Sharif in 2024**

Overall read: **negative, with some real but limited corrective / institutional positives**. Sharif’s 2024 record shows a few anti-corruption and transparency moves, but the stronger pattern is coercive information control, pressure on opposition and media, and institutional moves that reduced scrutiny. I did not find reliable 2024 proof of a new personal self-dealing episode; the stronger evidence is indirect: family influence, PM-centered control, and weak accountability.

**Accepted claims**

- `PM orders action over ‘ineffective’ track, trace system` — **Dawn**, `2024-05-08`, https://www.dawn.com/news/1832117  
  Claim: After an internal inquiry found the FBR’s track-and-trace system ineffective, Sharif ordered action against responsible officials. This is a genuine corrective signal and supports `7B.10` on the “models ethical standards” side.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.8`

- `Pakistan PM to choose banker Aurangzeb as finance minister, sources say` — **Reuters via ThePrint**, `2024-03-11`, https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-to-choose-banker-aurangzeb-as-finance-minister-sources-say/1996592/  
  Claim: Sharif chose a career banker, not a party loyalist, for finance. This supports a limited competence-and-credibility reading rather than outright patronage.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- `PM forms new Economic Advisory Council without Dar, Aurangzeb` — **The News**, `2024-05-19`, https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/1190715-pm-forms-new-economic-advisory-council-without-dar-aurangzeb  
  Claim: Sharif created an advisory council of economists, technocrats, and business figures for policy guidance. This is modest positive evidence for expert-led, less cynical policymaking.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- `PM Shehbaz directs full digitalization of social welfare payments under BISP` — **APP**, `2024-03-18`, https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-directs-full-digitalization-of-social-welfare-payments-under-bisp/  
  Claim: Moving BISP payments to digital wallets was explicitly framed as reducing leakage, delay, and discretion. That is concrete anti-clientelism and anti-patronage delivery reform.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- `PM orders crackdown on sugar mills, dealers` — **The Express Tribune**, `2024-11-19`, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2510586/pm-shehbaz-orders-crackdown-on-sugar-mills-dealers-along-with-cctv-surveillance?amp=1  
  Claim: Sharif ordered action against sugar mills and dealers for tax evasion, undocumented sales, and hoarding, including CCTV surveillance and joint enforcement. This is a useful counterpoint to any claim that he only protected sectoral insiders.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- `PM orders action against sugar mills` — **Dawn**, `2024-11-20`, https://www.dawn.com/news/1873622  
  Claim: Dawn reported Sharif said the sugar sector should be closely regulated and that mill owners involved in evasion and hoarding would face strict legal action. This again supports a limited anti-rent / pro-accountability reading.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- `Pakistan to investigate army's meddling in judiciary, law minister says` — **Reuters via Al Jazeera**, `2024-03-28`, https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/3/28/pakistan-to-investigate-armys-meddling-in-judiciary-law-minister-says  
  Claim: The government said it would form an inquiry commission after judges alleged intimidation by the ISI. That is the clearest positive evidence that Sharif’s government at least sometimes allowed politically sensitive investigations to proceed.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.8`, `7B.9`

- `Pakistan: Widening Crackdown on Dissent` — **Human Rights Watch**, `2024-01-11`, https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent  
  Claim: HRW said the government clamped down on dissenting media, opposition, and NGOs, and that journalists faced intimidation and surveillance. This is strong evidence against ethical, trust-building governance.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- `Social media platform X blocked in Pakistan over national security, ministry says` — **Reuters via Investing.com**, `2024-04-17`, https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313  
  Claim: The interior ministry confirmed X was blocked around the election period on national-security grounds, restricting reporting and monitoring at a sensitive moment. This reads as self-serving information control, not ethical transparency.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.8`, `7B.9`

- `Pakistan's government curbs judiciary's power after alleged harassment of MPs` — **The Guardian**, `2024-10-21`, https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps  
  Claim: Critics said the 26th Amendment weakened judicial independence and passed amid intimidation and abduction allegations. That is strong evidence against a ruler model of ethical restraint and independent accountability.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- `Human Rights Reports: Custom Report Excerpts` — **U.S. Department of State**, `2024`, https://2021-2025.state.gov/report/custom/69e9647867/  
  Claim: The report says journalists were pressured toward a predetermined narrative, and PEMRA/PTA/FIA tools were used to suppress threatening information. This is direct evidence of state-backed concealment and media pressure.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- `A dangerous digital crackdown` — **Human Rights Watch**, `2024-12-12`, https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/12/dangerous-digital-crackdown  
  Claim: HRW said internet throttling, VPN restrictions, and PECA-based controls were expanding, while a new agency was being built to police online content. This is strong evidence of normalizing censorship and state control rather than trust-building ethics.  
  IDs: `7B.10`, `7B.9`

**Search gap**

- I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence of a fresh, directly documented personal self-dealing scandal involving Sharif himself.
- The best 2024 evidence for the negative side is therefore indirect but substantial: family influence over appointments, PM-centered control, media restriction, and weakened judicial independence.
- The strongest positive evidence is also limited: targeted anti-evasion / anti-hoarding actions, technocratic appointments, and one inquiry commission. These are real but do not outweigh the broader pattern of coercive control and information suppression.
